title: Starting Strength - novice program review (ft. Pepe)
summary: He reviews Starting Strength for hypertrophy. Its minimalism suits novices, but it is really a powerlifting program with too much squatting, technical power cleans and huge movement-pattern gaps. A frog that wandered into his garage interrupts mid-review.
claims: You want high movement pattern selection with medium to low exercise selection; Starting Strength is low on both
Minimalism suits novices because repeating movements ingrains them neurologically before real muscle gains begin
Static rep ranges are fine for novices because weight on the bar keeps progressing regardless
One set of 5 deadlifts is excellent for novices: clean technique, decent volume, without wrecking recovery
Starting Strength is a powerlifting program and should not be called a novice program; not every novice wants to be a baby powerlifter
Old bodybuilder novice programs were just as bad with only isolation movements; powerlifters do not own compound movements
Squat obsession creates naturals with dominant quads and little else, the frog physique, so squat volume can be reduced
Bench 3x5 with only one day of rest between sessions may cause shoulder injuries in novices with poor technique
Monday-Wednesday-Friday is probably the best frequency for novices, with 45-60 minute sessions since they lack work capacity
Do not give a novice a laundry list; have them do effective compounds, get their tonnage and go home

He dislikes power cleans for hypertrophy and novices: very technical, need a solid front rack, most people's elbow and wrist positions are garbage, and you cannot reverse engineer them without learning the clean first
Football coaches should have players deadlift instead of power clean
Doing power cleans after deadlifts in phase 3 is better since you are warmed up, especially thoracic extension
Calisthenics such as chin-ups matter for novices because moving your body through space is an important skill
As a self-described triple weakling who started very low, a calisthenics phase helped him build a base for his base and may reduce injury
Calisthenics humble you: if you cannot do 10 clean push-ups, your bench number means you are regressing in athleticism

Starting Strength has too much knee flexion and lacks elbow flexion, wrist flexion, horizontal pulls, calf, neck, ab and hyperextension work; long head triceps, rear delts and upper back are neglected
Horizontal pulls are the least important movement pattern in his opinion
A novice program should teach a wide range of movement patterns so lifters know what they are doing on the next program
Restructure to two knee flexions, two hip hinges and two horizontal presses per week, freeing three slots for a curl, a triceps movement and a hyperextension
Include some fun; endless squat, bench and deadlift makes many novices quit
It pushes strength progression too fast to rush novices out; the novice phase should be one of discovery before specialising
exercises: shoulder risk with one rest day
too technical for hypertrophy and novices
